title: 2012 HMMT February Geometry Problem 4
statement: There are circles \(\omega_{1}\) and \(\omega_{2}\). They intersect in two points, one of which is the point \(A\). \(B\) lies on \(\omega_{1}\) such that \(A B\) is tangent to \(\omega_{2}\). The tangent to \(\omega_{1}\) at \(B\) intersects \(\omega_{2}\) at \(C\) and \(D\), where \(D\) is the closer to \(B\). \(A D\) intersects \(\omega_{1}\) again at \(E\). If \(B D=3\) and \(C D=13\), find \(E B / E D\).

solutions.text:
\(4 \sqrt{3} / 3\)

> [diagram]

By power of a point, \(B A=\sqrt{B D \cdot B C}=4 \sqrt{3}\). Also, \(D E B \sim D B A\), so \(E B / E D=B A / B D=4 \sqrt{3} / 3\).
